I haven't read any crime thrillers, detective stories or murder mystery books but wouldn't mind trying a good one out. What do you recommend?

The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes are my favorite collection of stories in the detective genre. I'm not much for murder mysteries or thrillers, but I love the sense of constant deduction that you get in a good detective book. The Sherlock Holmes books are also a collection of relatively short stories, so they're a little more bite-sized than other books.

Edit: I'm also midway through "Lockwood and Co" series, by Jonathan Stroud. It's set in a universe where ghosts haunt murder sites and other sites of tragic death, and where some children have the ability to see and hear the ghosts at work. These children are often pushed into the role of "Psychical investigators", trying to dispel the ghosts by any means necessary. Lockwood and Co is unique because their company of physical investigators is interested in solving the mystery behind a person's death rather than just getting rid of the ghost. The characters are memorable and the storytelling is good, and you get the same sense of "ah ha!" that you get from Sherlock Holmes, although it's often one big case to be cracked rather than a series of smaller deductions leading to a whole.
I will have to find some Sherlock to read then. Any story in particular stand out to you?

If you're after longer stories, The Hound of The Baskervilles is a good one. If you're like me and enjoy the shorter stories, I've always liked "The Red Headed League", "A Case of Identity," and "A Scandal in Bohemia". The best thing about Holmes mysteries is that you're usually given all the clues that Holmes is, so you can attempt to solve the mystery before the big reveal. It bugs me when I'm watching a detective show and the protagonist solves the mystery using details we weren't privy to ahead of time; it's much more satisfying when I realize the clues were there all along, I just didn't put them together the correct way.

Sci-fi is a surprisingly huge genre (with many sub-genres) it would be REALLY helpful if you could explain a bit about other stuff you do like or what interests you about this genre. With that said, here's a few of my favorites:

  • Diamond Age by Neal Stephenson
  • Harrison Bergeron (amazing short story, more dystopian than sci-fi but I think it qualifies)
  • The Book of the New Sun
  • Dune
  • The Hyperion Cantos
  • Ilium/Olympos
  • Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy (more of a comedy but quite definitely sci-fi settings)

I generaly like books with a rich universe that sucks me into it, with psycological insight and social or individual criticism. The mix between philosophy and a read that makes you feel inside of the story is what atracts me. What interests me in sci-fi, as a guess (since ive read probably one, 1984), is the unknown adventure into futuristic places and concepts, and greatly developed universes.

Dune or The Book of the New Sun for sure then. Both have insanely deep universes with quite a bit of insight that can be taken away from either.

Out of the two, Dune is (in my opinion) by far and away the more accessible to read. There's a ton of supplementary information from the fanbase and any questions you have could be pretty easily answered on Google.

The Book of the New Sun is absolutely amazing but it requires quite a bit of work on the reader's part as the writing style describes things in medieval terms but it's set billions of years into the future when our sun is beginning to go cold. I believe the thought process on the author's part was that it's so far out of our frame of reference that he may as well put it in a different, but somewhat more familiar, frame. Ends up being a hell of a read either way.
